title: Caulaincourt to Napoleon, Congress of Châtillon, February-March 1814: the undeciphered letter of 25 Feb 1814 (AN AF/IV/1676 no. 131) and its keyed siblings nos. 130 and 170-171 (catalogue 534)

documents.shelfmark: Archives nationales, AF/IV/1676, plaquette 4/III no. 131, ff. 890-892 (served on microfilm, Pierrefitte)
documents.route: Armand de Caulaincourt, duke of Vicenza, Châtillon-sur-Seine -> Napoleon I

plaintext.source: AN inventory: 'Lettre en grande partie chiffrée (et sans le déchiffrement)'. No decipherment on or with the leaves (checked on the microfilm, 7 Nov 2026). The opening (f. 890r) and the closing formula are in clear.

transcription.source: Phone photographs of the microfilm reader screen taken by Jean-Loko, 7 Nov 2026 (14 photos); not committed, held by the contributor
transcription.notes: Two independent readings (A: Claude Opus 5.5; B: Claude Sonnet 5.5), reconciled by scripts/consensus.py: 94% of groups agree, 24 open disagreements listed in the consensus file. Reading A numbers the f. 890v lines from the clear line (its L02 = B's L01).

documents.shelfmark: Archives nationales, AF/IV/1676, plaquette 4/III no. 130, f. 884r-v (continues on f. 885, not photographed)
documents.route: Armand de Caulaincourt, Châtillon-sur-Seine -> Napoleon I

plaintext.source: Contemporary decipherment written under each cipher line (not mentioned by the AN inventory, which describes no. 130 as a letter)

transcription.source: Phone photographs of the microfilm reader screen, Jean-Loko, 7 Nov 2026 (6 photos)
transcription.notes: Two independent readings (Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5), 95% agreement on the groups; interlinear text and word positions (P lines) from reading A.

documents.shelfmark: Archives nationales, AF/IV/1676, plaquette 4/IV no. 170, ff. 969-973 (the inventory gives f. 968)
documents.route: Armand de Caulaincourt, Châtillon-sur-Seine -> Napoleon I

plaintext.source: No. 171 (ff. 974-976) is its contemporary decipherment; a pale pencil decipherment, word by word, also runs under most cipher lines (not mentioned by the inventory)

transcription.source: Phone photographs of the microfilm reader screen, Jean-Loko, 7 Nov 2026 (28 photos)
transcription.notes: Two independent readings (Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5): 83% agreement; the moiré of the screen confuses 2/7, 4/8 and 3/5. Pencil glosses read in part (transcriptions/n170_gloss_anchors.tsv).

system.summary: Numeric nomenclator to about 1200, groups separated by dots, some underlined. Whole words (paix, que, les, pour, dans), syllables (Bassano = 952 959/663 395) and some letters; homophones for frequent words (que = 264, 669, 1191); nulls likely. The same key serves no. 130 (25 Feb) and no. 170 (6 Mar).
system.sibling_key: Nos. 130 (interlinear decipherment) and 170-171 (separate decipherment) in the same carton; plaquettes 4/III-4/IV hold further pairs (161-169, 173-177) and interlinear decipherments (169bis, 179, 185, 187) not yet photographed
system.notes: distinct_symbols counts the different numbers met in nos. 130 and 170 together. Key order: frequent words get unrelated numbers (que 264/669/1191, de 574, les 788), so the table is not alphabetical as far as checked.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherments of nos. 130 (interlinear) and 170 (no. 171, and pencil glosses) in the same carton; none known for no. 131. Fain, Manuscrit de 1814 (1823), appendix no. 29 prints a different letter of 6 Mar 1814 in clear (candidate for no. 172).

conditions.human_role: Contributed: Jean-Loko consulted AF/IV/1676 on microfilm at the Archives nationales (Pierrefitte) on 7 Nov 2026 and photographed the reader screen; the transcriptions (two independent readings per cipher), their reconciliation and the key alignment were done with Claude Code.

solution.what: AF/IV/1676 consulted on microfilm at Pierrefitte; nos. 130, 131, 170 and 171 photographed from the reader screen (the call number comes from the AN inventory FRAN_IR_003828: plaquettes 4/III and 4/IV are both in AF/IV/1676).

Each cipher read twice independently from the photographs and reconciled group by group: no. 130 95%, no. 131 94%, no. 170 83% agreement. No. 171 (970 words) and the clear opening of no. 131 transcribed.

Fain, Manuscrit de 1814, appendix no. 29 prints a Caulaincourt letter of 6 Mar 1814 ('La question qui va se décider...'), not the text of no. 171. Houssaye, 1814 (1888) quotes Caulaincourt's letters of 24 and 27 Feb and 1, 11 and 13 Mar from 'Arch. des Affaires étrangères, fonds France, 668'.

Shared key rebuilt by soft EM alignment of no. 170 with no. 171 (pencil glosses as anchors) and of no. 130 line by line with its interlinear text (word positions as anchors), uncertain readings kept as candidate sets (scripts/aligner_multi.py).
The values written by the decipherer of no. 130 (798 par, 84 en, 904 une, 910 lettre, 800 à, 18 et) are those found independently in the 170-171 alignment: one key for 25 Feb and 6 Mar.
Partial key applied to no. 131: 140 of 481 groups take a firm value; the result does not build sentences (key/n131_trial_decode.txt).

outcome.method_basis: A partial key (582 numbers aligned, 105 with a firm value) was rebuilt from the contemporary decipherments of nos. 130 and 170 in the same key; applied to no. 131 it gives values for under a third of the groups and no sentences.

gaps.detail: the partial key covers too little: 83% of its numbers occur in nos. 130 and 170 but only 29% have a firm value; more decipherments in the same key are in the carton (169bis, 179, 185, 187 interlinear; pairs 161-169, 173-177; f. 885 of no. 130)
not photographed; it follows no. 171, so it starts at f. 977 (the inventory's ff. 974-981 include no. 171). Compare with Fain no. 29 (print/fain1823_no29_6mar1814.txt)

gaps.item: Clear copies of the Châtillon letters
gaps.detail: Houssaye's 'Affaires étrangères, fonds France, 668' (probably Mémoires et documents, France 668, La Courneuve) may hold the clear texts
phone photographs of the reader screen; 17% of groups uncertain (2/7, 4/8, 3/5). Exporting images from the reader should settle most
